questions.question: Where should cargo be placed to help prevent a rollover?

options.text: As high as possible inside a trailer.
As low as possible inside a trailer.
On the driver's side of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible inside a trailer.
questions.explanation: Placing cargo low reduces the risk of rollover. A vehicle that is too heavy at the top is more likely to tip over.

questions.question: On a shipping paper with both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how are hazardous materials identified?
questions.correctAnswerText: Listed first.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials on a shipping paper must be clearly identified. They may be listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" before the description.

questions.question: What must a driver do when crossing railroad tracks with an empty hazardous materials cargo tank?

options.text: Should not cross a railroad crossing.
Needs to slow down but is not required to stop.
Must stop at a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with cargo tanks for hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks. This rule applies whether the tanks are full or empty.

questions.question: Why can opening trailer doors during a cargo fire make the fire worse?

options.text: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
It changes the temperature of the trailer.
It provides more moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: Opening doors during a cargo fire allows oxygen to enter. This can cause the fire to flare up and spread.

questions.question: What should you do with belts during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Leave them alone and do not inspect them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them for tightness.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check all belts for tightness and wear. Learn the correct amount of slack for each belt.

questions.question: In extremely hot weather, what should you do if tire air pressure is too high?

options.text: Let the tires cool before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the tires cool before driving.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, which can cause tire pressure to reach dangerous levels. Stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as pressure will drop too low once they cool down.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Use mirrors regularly when turning, changing lanes, merging, and doing tight maneuvers. Do not use mirrors to check fuel prices.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot potential vehicle problems?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during your trip, not just at the start and end. Watch the gauges, use your senses, and look at tires, cargo, and lights. Be alert for any sign of trouble.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop a safe distance away, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a safe distance away, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: Stop a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive driver's behavior that you witnessed.

questions.question: What does it mean if "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers?

options.text: An inhalation hazard placard is required only for loads over 100 pounds.
An inhalation hazard placard is required for any amount of the material.
Air masks must be provided to anyone handling the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: An inhalation hazard placard is required for any amount of the material.
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package or shipping paper, you must display the proper inhalation hazard placard and any other required placards. This applies regardless of the amount being transported.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that should concern drivers?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Drivers and pedestrians talking to someone may be distracted and not watching the road. Workers on or near the road may focus on their work instead of traffic, and they can also distract drivers.

questions.question: When are people usually the least alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night, especially after midnight. Crashes from tired driving happen more often at night than at any other time.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth required for rear tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Check your tires for at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove on the front tires, and at least 2/32 of an inch on other tires. All tires on the same vehicle should be the same size.

questions.question: When driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within reach
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials, keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another easy-to-reach location while wearing your seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes
questions.explanation: Braking after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes if possible until your vehicle slows down a lot.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, the seals should be pressed together at what angle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 90 degrees
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect the correct glad hands. The seals should be pressed together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, the trailer should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing

questions.correctAnswerText: Cleaned with water
questions.explanation: Parts of a vehicle that touch corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, they should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Secure
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, check wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and that they are properly attached. Clean the blades if they are dirty.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Only happens at very high speeds
Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph
Happens most often when tire pressure is too high

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or tire tread is worn.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under an upcoming bridge, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. Find an alternate route if possible.
